title: GitHub Release notes are read from the operator's working-tree CHANGELOG, not the tagged commit (pair with quest-cli)
description: Found by the LCLI-622 reviewer (opum-workflow:reviewer, branch feat/LCLI-622-executed-github-release at 30571a09, 2026-09-28). This is a design point shared with quest, not a regression. scripts/github-release.mjs releaseNotesFor reads join(root, 'CHANGELOG.md') from the checkout promote-latest.mjs runs in. So an uncommitted edit, or an edit landed after the tag, becomes the body of a NEW vX release, and nothing checks the notes against the tagged commit. An EXISTING release is safe: differing notes are refused and never edited. Sections do get edited after release. The reviewer's live comparison: v0.11.0, 0.9.3, 0.9.2, 0.9.1, 0.8.0, 0.7.0, 0.6.2 and 0.6.0 match their current CHANGELOG sections, while v0.9.0 and v0.6.1 do not. The LCLI-622 pairing recorded this as MATCH with quest-cli QCLI-398 (both read the working tree), so changing it is a paired change. Suggested rule: read CHANGELOG.md from the commit v<X> peels to (git show <peeled>:CHANGELOG.md, a commit promote-latest.mjs already resolves in step 1), for both the pre-move refusal and the cut. Also noted, theoretical: a '## ' line inside a fenced code block would silently truncate a section, in both repos' extractors.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The rule is agreed with quest-cli, and both sides read the release notes from the tagged commit rather than the working tree, for both the pre-move check and the cut
A test proves a working-tree CHANGELOG edit that is not in the tagged commit does not reach the release body
bun test and bun run lore check exit 0; a reviewer pass covers the scripts/ change

implementationNotes: PAIRED (2026-09-28). quest-cli filed the twin as QCLI-407, same shape: read the notes via git show <peeled>:CHANGELOG.md for both the pre-move refusal and the cut. In quest, the notes are read at promote-release.mjs:813, after resolveTagCommit at :691 (quest-cli's reading, not re-resolved here). QCLI-407 also covers the fenced '## ' truncation edge, and names one asymmetry: quest's changelogSection does not CRLF-normalise the CHANGELOG, while lore's does. Its AC4 is a by-ref cross-read at both final heads. Neither side has scheduled it; send lore's plan or head to quest-cli when this starts.
